podcast_name: More Than Money with Gene Dickison
question: What should investors do after election market volatility to avoid derailing their long-term strategy?
transcript_excerpt: Remember that you're not going to make long-term strategy changes based on short-term events. As long as the fundamentals remain the same, stick to your plan. The stock market generally runs on emotion and short-term volatility is absolutely irrelevant. Historically, in the year following an election, the markets are up.

podcast_name: More Than Money with Gene Dickison
question: Why did markets react negatively to midterm election results and political uncertainty?
transcript_excerpt: Markets hate uncertainty. The sell-off was driven by uncertainty about how political changes will affect companies spending and profitability, particularly in the AI data center realm. This got worse because of automated systems that trade in response to market activity.

podcast_name: More Than Money with Gene Dickison
question: What were gasoline and crude oil price movements in the week following the November midterm election?
transcript_excerpt: Crude oil prices dropped about nine percent on Wednesday, then went up three percent on Thursday. Gasoline prices are down 7% over three weeks, though still at levels where four dollars per gallon feels expensive.
